That rests on a readers' poll. Not on sales.

beats.narr: Cambridge Dictionary has chosen its word of the year.
The word is 'human'.
It means having the faults and feelings people have.

n261118j.end: Gary is admitted as human, on faults alone.
n261118j.title: Point of order: is Gary one?
n261118j.claim: Cambridge Dictionary named 'human' its word of the year, saying the growth of AI means people now have to say 'human' for things that once only humans could do.
n261118j.why: The dictionary defines it as having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines. Compounds such as human-made are rising too.
facts: The word of the year: 'human'
Its use has grown four-fold since 1900
In English since the 14th century, from French
Rising too: 'human-made' and 'human-driven'
Chief editor: AI made it necessary to say it
